items.title: Rome judges set to give verdict in Regeni murder trial
items.description: (ANSA) - ROME, 28 SET - Judges in a Rome court on Monday retired to deliberate on their verdict in the trial of four Egyptian national security officials over the abduction and torturing to death of Italian student Giulio Regeni in Cairo in January-February 2016. The verdict is expected at around 6 pm Italian time. The 28-year-old student's half-naked body was found in a ditch on the Cairo-Alexandria highway on February 3, 2016, nine days after he disappeared on the Cairo metro on January 25. Regeni, a Friuli-born Cambridge University doctoral researcher into Cairo street unions, was allegedly
items.titleIt: Rome judges set to give verdict in Regeni murder trial

items.description: Residents reported hearing a series of powerful explosions across Baidoa, with thick plumes of smoke visible over parts of the city. items.title: Hunger and malnutrition crises persist in Somalia as projected floods and funding shortfalls threaten vulnerable populations
items.description: The Federal Government of Somalia and the United Nations warn that projected flooding and funding shortfalls could worsen the hunger crisis and push more people – especially children -- into extreme food insecurity and acute malnutrition.   The latest Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC)* analysis projects that 5.4 million people will face crisis levels of hunger or worse between October and December 2026, including 1.5 million people facing emergency levels of hunger or worse. items.titleIt: Hunger and malnutrition crises persist in Somalia as projected floods and funding shortfalls threaten vulnerable populations

items.title: Ten Years On, Somalia's Lower Shabelle's Farmers Still Can't Go Home: A Decade of War, Land Disputes, and Aid That Never Reaches Far Enough
items.description: It was the latest wave in a displacement crisis that has been building in Somalia's Lower Shabelle region for a decade, and there is no sign it is reversing. Aadan Rooble knows the pattern well. He walked for part of the ten days it took him to reach Mogadishu after airstrikes made the decision for him — the farm his family worked in the village of Farxaano was no longer somewhere anyone could stay. His sons now find casual work when they can. He doesn't expect to go home. He's one of tens of thousands of farmers who have fled Somalia's Lower Shabelle region over the past decade, arriving in M
items.titleIt: Ten Years On, Somalia's Lower Shabelle's Farmers Still Can't Go Home: A Decade of War, Land Disputes, and Aid That Never Reaches Far Enough

items.title: Somali journalist Mohamed Aweys Muudey stabbed to death in exile in Germany
items.description: According to a joint press release from the Darmstadt Public Prosecutor's Office and the South Hesse Police Headquarters, Mohamed Aweys Muudey, 68, an asylum seeker who had fled Somalia, was stabbed inside his communal accommodation by a 28-year-old suspect who is now in police custody. Muudey left Somalia in search of safety and protection. However, his life was cut short in a violent knife attack, highlighting the dangers many journalists in exile continue to face. items.title: SJS mourns Somali radio journalist Hassan Kafi Qoyste who died at 57
items.description: Ayanle Hassan, Qoyste's son, told SJS that his father, who was diabetic, fell ill on Friday night and was rushed to hospital, where he was pronounced dead. The late Qoyste was a veteran journalist and one of the most remarkable radio journalists in Somalia, known for his distinctive and memorable voice. He first worked as an archive manager at the Ministry of Labour of the Somali central government in the 1980s before joining the print media in Mogadishu in the early 1990s, as the country descended into civil war. items.title: Somalia: NISA Arrests 11 Al-Shabaab Operatives in Security Operations Around Mogadishu
items.description: NISA said its forces arrested 11 operatives linked to the networks, which were allegedly being prepared to carry out activities threatening security. The networks were dismantled during planned security operations conducted in Darussalam, Garasbaley, Kahda, Daynile, and Afgoye. NISA forces also seized weapons and other materials that the operatives allegedly intended to use in their planned activities. The operations are part of NISA's ongoing efforts to prevent Al-Shabaab and other terrorist groups from carrying out activities aimed at undermining security and harming the Somali people.
items.titleIt: Somalia: NISA Arrests 11 Al-Shabaab Operatives in Security Operations Around Mogadishu

items.description: The group that arrived in Mogadishu reportedly comprised 25 men and 25 women. The deportees are said to have been living in Turkey for various reasons, including education and employment, while some were reportedly suspected of involvement in irregular migration or attempts to travel onward to Europe. items.titleIt: Somali-Turkish Tensions Rise as Deportations Follow Anti-Ankara Protests

items.title: Somali journalist Mohamed Aweys Muudey stabbed to death in exile in Germany
items.description: According to a joint press release from the Darmstadt Public Prosecutor's Office and the South Hesse Police Headquarters, Mohamed Aweys Muudey, 68, an asylum seeker who had fled Somalia, was stabbed inside his communal accommodation by a 28-year-old suspect who is now in police custody. Muudey left Somalia in search of safety and protection. However, his life was cut short in a violent knife attack, highlighting the dangers many journalists in exile continue to face. He spent several years in prison in Ethiopia where he was arrested while seeking protection in 2014 before he was pardoned. Muud

items.description: The incident reportedly occurred at a residential facility. German authorities have identified a 28-year-old Somali man as the suspect.
